_notice: Verdicts on the two lot-source supplier names that reach two rows on one framework's own brief supplier list. Written 18/11/2026.
rule: The brief's supplier list is a capture of the owner's published page, verified against that page's own stated supplier count, and is never edited to resolve a Hub-side ambiguity. A lot attaches to a brief row only where the seed holds BOTH the notice's name and that row verbatim on one record.

frameworks.why: Two real companies, not one row printed twice. The notice names "Clinisupplies Limited", the registered name of 04013240, the company the Hub's Clinisupplies record resolves to, and that record holds both that name and the "Clinisupplies Ltd" row verbatim. No row was picked any other way.
frameworks.residual: SETTLED 18/11/2026, later the same day. 02503030 now has its own Hub record, "Clinisupplies GB Limited" (added by scripts/_add_clinisupplies_gb_record_1118.py), holding Lots 1, 2, 3, 5 and 13 off this same notice under its then-name Great Bear Healthcare Ltd. It is still NOT an alias of 04013240 and must never become one — different registration numbers are evidence they are distinct. On Lou's ruling ("Two records + link", 18/11/2026) the relationship between the two is published as a sourced fact on each record rather than resolved by a merge: see deepDive.ownership on both, written by scripts/_add_clinisupplies_group_link_1118.py, which gives the persons-with-significant-control chain read at Companies House on 18/11/2026 — both registrations sit under CLINISUPPLIES GROUP LIMITED 14506446 up to KKR & Co. Inc., 75% or more at every link, 02503030 via GREAT BEAR HEALTHCARE GROUP LIMITED 12570444. One business, two live registrations. Common ownership is not one legal person, and this notice awards them as two supplier parties (GB-FTS-96951 and GB-FTS-96957) on different lots, which is why the records stay apart and this verdict is unchanged. What remains open is only the normaliser: company_match.key() still strips the "GB", so a bare "Clinisupplies" resolves AMBIGUOUS and each record is kept apart by the verbatim tier in company_match.resolve() and app/company-report.js. Narrowing key() would move award routing repo-wide, so it stays a separate question. test_previous_names.py records the pair in SETTLED_DISTINCT.

frameworks.why: Also two real rows, not a duplicate, so there is nothing to de-duplicate. frameworks.whatWouldChangeIt: NHS Supply Chain printing the entity in full on the brief, or a Find a Tender notice naming the awardee with its registration number.
